correctness.rationale: For each k the two independent depolarizing maps give four explicit positive-semidefinite components, with partial transpose having k(k-1)/2 mutually orthogonal 2-by-2 blocks. Their negative eigenvalue is exactly [d^2(1-p)(1-q)-d(p(1-q)+q(1-p))-kpq]_+/(kd^2), with all other eigenvalues nonnegative. Summation gives the stated exact negativity for all integer d>=3, k=1..d and p,q in [0,1]. The untruncated rank score is a strictly discretely concave quadratic when pq>0; its adjacent difference is Delta-2kpq. For p=q=t, the substitution x=d(1-t)/t turns each switch into x=1+sqrt(2k+1). Exact boundary cases, all-zero region, and pq=0 are handled separately; representative full-matrix checker confirms the algebra but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 anchor specifically compares dimensional robustness of entanglement generated from high-dimensional coherence and emphasizes that global depolarization shifts partial-transpose blocks by a uniform floor. Independent local depolarization is a physically natural missing comparison; it qualitatively changes how flat-support coherence should be allocated. The theorem gives exact two-rate quantitative negativities, an all-dimension sequence of genuine interior optimal ranks, and a concrete qutrit separation N_2=1/72>N_3=0 at equal half-depolarization. This supplies a reproducible rank-selection rule in an experimentally motivated state-preparation family, not an arbitrary slice or mere rediscovery of the old entanglement-death endpoint.
